questionText:
Read the following excerpt carefully and answer the question that follows:

"Ibn Battuta was fascinated by plants that were completely unfamiliar to his North African audience. Describing the coconut, he wrote: 'These trees are among the most peculiar trees in the world... The nut of a coconut tree resembles a human head, for in it are what look like two eyes and a mouth, and inside, when it is green, there is what looks like brains, and within it which is like hair. They make from this cordage with which they sew up ships instead of iron nails.' Describing the betel (paan), he noted: 'The betel is a tree which is cultivated in the same manner as the grape-vine... The betel has no fruit and is grown only for the sake of its leaves... The manner of its use is that before eating it one takes the areca nut, which is like a nutmeg, breaks it into small pellets and puts these in his mouth and chews them. Then he takes the leaves of betel, puts a little chalk (lime) on them, and chews them together.'"

topic: Francois Bernier on Property in Land
questionText:
Read the following excerpt carefully and answer the question that follows:

"Francois Bernier, a French physician and philosopher who spent twelve years in India (1656–1668), addressed an influential letter to Jean-Baptiste Colbert, the French Minister of Finance under Louis XIV. Bernier argued: 'The king is the sole and absolute proprietor of all the land in the empire... Hence it follows that there is no private property in land... As the ground is seldom tilled otherwise than by compulsion, and as no person is interested in sustaining the productivity of the soil, the country is neglected, agriculture falls to decay, and the peasantry is impoverished. The houses are wretched hovels, and the cities are little more than military camps.' Bernier warned King Louis XIV never to adopt the oriental system of state land ownership."
